pr_title: Preserve original name in shader params cache
pr_body: Fixes #50936, which was a regression from #50511.

issue_context.title: [Godot4] shader param not effect
issue_context.body:

shader param not effect

### Steps to reproduce

run reproduction project

comments: Seems like all shader uniforms are broken due to recent rendering changes. cc @reduz (I'm not very familiar with rendering Vulkan API)
Same problem here I think... I've got a shader that samples a heightmap and its just showing flat now.
Just to toss my hat in the ring, can also confirm using Nvidia Studio drivers for Windows 10. It is not possible to make shaders with custom uniforms with the latest builds.

@darrylryan @Ace-Dragon Could you try to [bisect the regression](https://docs.godotengine.org/en/latest/community/contributing/bisecting_regressions.html) to see when the issue started happening?

The `good` commit is likely something like `HEAD~500` (500 commits prior to latest `master`), whereas the `bad` commit is https://github.com/godotengine/godot/commit/e6a544c169ae598c1a6f8632f6d8bed1abcdaddc.

So far I've narrowed it to:

cf3f404d312146cf46ae27fd8d220852eac27eb9 bad
c25fa02c1c242df0f256dd58af650f8c8806c066 good

96d7bc62af25b85b8b9cc091eeea1e7a784ba624 seems to be the one that breaks it for me... the previous commit my heightmap image is sampled correctly by the shader, with this one in the terrain is just flat.

review_comments: Yep, sorry about the quick merge - but I've really quite tired of this bug, and this PR really fixes it.

@akien-mga in either case ``pi`` is modified before it is stored in p_params. So that is likely not an issue. The real issue is that the copy of the Property info stored in local  (e.g. the copy returned by ``RenderingServer::get_singleton()->shader_get_param_list(shader, &local);``) will be incorrectly changed. 

Although, now that I think about it. I remember JFons talking about this new iterator approach creating copies unless we added const or something. Perhaps this iterator is making a copy of ``pi`` anyway?
